analysis:
Both units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 427-597 and 598-781). The input has no patch hunks or head text, so I could not identify what this PR changes; this is a coverage limit, not evidence that the change is safe. The base text is documentation only and has no code, no authorization path and no executable behaviour. I report no findings.

The excerpts describe security-relevant behaviours that the later source and integration passes should check against the actual code diff:
- SSD prefix-cache TTL raised from 15 to 30 minutes, with the SEC-035 re-acceptance (T-041).
- SSD write budget raised to 750 GB/day.
- Cache routing state persisted across coordinator restarts.
- App Attest protocol-3-only serving, key rotation limits, and build qualification/revocation (T-052 to T-058, TB-011).
- Removal of the unauthenticated /v1/provider/earnings route (T-031).
- Attestation challenges now fail closed.
- MIN_PROVIDER_VERSION now excludes providers that report no version.
- Removal of Python-era wire fields.
- Public model-demand aggregates published with cohort suppression (at least 20 requests and 3 accounts).
- Cached-token pricing.

If later PR units touch code behind these claims, check that the claims match the code. In particular, check that fail-closed behaviour, the 30-minute TTL maximum, the per-request authorization re-checks at dispatch, and the suppression thresholds are implemented as described.
